ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, two parallel metal rails are placed horizontally with a distance of $l=0.50\mathrm{m}$ between them. The left end is connected to a resistor $R=0.2\Omega$. A uniform magnetic field with magnetic induction $B=0.40\mathrm{T}$ is directed perpendicularly downward to the plane of the rails. A conductor rod $ac$ (with length $l$) is placed vertically on the rails and can slide frictionlessly along them. The resistance of the rails and the conductor rod can be neglected. When the rod $ac$ slides horizontally to the right at a constant speed of $v=4.0\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$, find:

1. The magnitude of the induced electromotive force in the AC rod
2. The magnitude of the induced current in the circuit
3. The magnitude of the horizontal external force required to maintain the uniform motion of the $ac$ rod.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there are two parallel metal rails forming the upper and lower horizontal sides; the left end is connected to a resistor R, and on the right side there is a vertical conducting rod ac bridging between the two rails, with a velocity arrow v pointing to the right beside the conducting rod. In the figure, multiple crosses indicate that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of the rails and directed inward; on the right side, the distance l between the two rails is marked. The whole forms a closed rectangular circuit composed of the resistor on the left side, the upper and lower rails, and the moving conducting rod ac. Reasoning: The problem gives l=0.50 m, B=0.40 T, v=4.0 m/s, R=0.2 Ω, and the resistance of the rails and the conducting rod is neglected. The magnitude of the motional electromotive force generated by the moving conducting rod cutting magnetic field lines is ε=Blv=0.40×0.50×4.0=0.8 V. The total resistance of the closed circuit is R=0.2 Ω, so the magnitude of the induced current is I=ε/R=0.8/0.2=4 A. After the moving rod carries current, it is subject to a magnetic resistance force in the magnetic field, whose magnitude is F=BIl=0.40×4×0.50=0.8 N. In order to maintain uniform motion to the right, the magnitude of the external force should be equal to the magnitude of this magnetic resistance force, and its direction is opposite to that of the magnetic resistance force.
